native_commit_protocol.before_call: Registry reserves slot and buffer/generation; all kinds/widths/epochs preinitialized, commit0/stage0. Native function pointer and args are prebound before invocation. Count scratch is initialized but its bits are not a count observation. Close right is consumed in kernel ledger before dispatch; no retry even for unknown/later failure.
native_commit_protocol.conversion: Native RAW_EXIT_PREPARED and conversion OBJECT_PREPARED are only prepared facts. Actual Python caller return lives in separate kernel first-visible cell. Conversion failure leaves all prior committed native axes intact and latches the same original exception before diagnostic formatting.
native_commit_protocol.count: Only ReadFile/WriteFile have count axis. The API writes a preallocated DWORD scratch; after scalar publication wrapper copies its actual contents into count.payload and commits before Python conversion. Committed count is raw postcall out-buffer content, not by itself defined byte progress. If native call has not returned/commit is absent, initialized or changed scratch stays unobserved/undefined.
native_commit_protocol.error: Raw last-error DWORD and legality/definedness are independent axes. Last-error is captured on the SAME calling thread immediately after useful documented return, with no intervening Win32/Python helper. Ordinary memory stores/fences are required not to alter it. Normal failure path can commit legalityTrue before the error transport returns; reverse partial observation is representable too. Success/nondocumented branch commitsFalse without reading stale last-error. A DWORD0 never means UNOBSERVED or automatically undefined.
native_commit_protocol.error_transport: GetLastError is named internal error transport, not an invented15th file port. Its actual wrapper work and trust/census belong to the future actor plan; no FormatMessage/SetLastError or other implicit export is added.
native_commit_protocol.interruption_limit: No atomic capture from OS return through CPU scheduling/SEH/process kill/ABI into memory is promised. Interrupted-before-commit remains unknown even if the OS completed. Release/acquire is a planned publication mechanism, not a proof against process termination or malicious native code. No pure stub/test brand qualifies native-first behavior.
native_commit_protocol.linearization: COMMITTED requires expected epoch/kind/width, payload then release commit, read with acquire after quiescence. Before commit raw payload bits are retained as provisional bytes but value authority remains UNKNOWN. Interruption after payload but before stage may still show UNOBSERVED with changed bits; NEVER promote those bits by guessing. Staged state is not a native-ready capability.
native_commit_protocol.no_reuse: One epoch per reserved call and one native dispatch; cells never overwritten/recycled in-session. Repeated reads/same-fact reconciliation are idempotent and do not doublefold; conflicting commit or stale/foreign ref stops work.
native_commit_protocol.scalar_first: After the target API returns, the FIRST intended application data store is the direct native-width result into scalar.payload, before error transport, Python/C API allocation, bool/count normalization, format packing or clock callback. For BOOL/DWORD write native32 bits into the prezeroed lowword, preserving2/-1/0; HANDLE writes64 bits. Only then stage_hint is set and aligned release commit publishes the axis.
